ticket.title: Client is experiencing repeated publishing failures and incorrect /case-studies Preview rendering despite valid saved files, and is requesting a technical review of Version 50 without any reset, rollback, or overwrite without approval.
ticket.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 15

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

<email>

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

I’m trying to successfully preview and publish my Acquisity AI Name 1 project, specifically ensuring that the saved Case Studies and Pricing pages render correctly at their respective routes and that the current Version 50 project can be published.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

I’ve completed extensive diagnostics and controlled testing with the Name 1 AI. I verified the affected page source, components, imports, data, routing configuration, and related files. I also performed an isolation test by temporarily replacing /app/case-studies/page.tsx with a simple static test page, then restored the original page exactly. I also created and saved the Pricing page and preserved a read-only snapshot of the affected source files. No further troubleshooting or code changes are currently being made.

#### What is happening instead?

Publishing repeatedly fails with the generic “Publishing failed. Please try again.” message. The /case-studies route either renders the Home page instead of its saved content or becomes completely black after reloading Preview. The same incorrect Home-page rendering previously occurred with the newly created /pricing route, although Pricing is now rendering correctly in Preview. The Preview toolbar correctly identifies the requested routes, and the underlying files appear to be saved and valid. This suggests there may be an issue with the current Version 50 preview/build/deployment state rather than the page source itself.

#### What is the expected outcome?

I’d like the technical team to inspect the Version 50 preview, build, and deployment state/logs, identify the underlying cause of the publishing failure and Case Studies rendering issue, and restore normal Preview and Publish functionality. Please contact me before performing any reset, rollback, regeneration, automated repair, or action that could overwrite the current project source, as substantial completed work is saved and preserved.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI Name 1 publish of <domain> fails with 'Publishing failed' after a failed production build, and the build error is never surfaced
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom conversation**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Testable claim**: A customer on a website whose custom domain <domain> shows verified and connected (website.domainVerified = true, domain_verified_at 2026-09-17T13:22:05Z) cannot publish version 26; every publish shows only "Publishing failed. Please try again." while version 19, the last successful deploy, still reports as published, so the button flips between Publish and Update. The site's production deployment is stuck at deployment_status = failed with deployment_error `Command "bun run build" exited with 1` (vercel_deployment_id dpl_5NoSQNGf5cxHXbZ9PovBartdYscX, updated 2026-09-18T15:54:36Z), and the customer reports no deployment logs to troubleshoot.

**Bounded conversation context**: Opened 2026-09-18 15:41 UTC, tagged AI Name 1, agent Fin AI then assigned to Name 2. The customer states: publishing changes throws "publishing failed"; there is no "Fix with AI" option; the panel shows only the generic "Publishing failed. Please try again."; "We could not load your domain ownership"; the last successful deploy was version 19 (the first publish), selecting version 19 shows published and the button reads Update, while selecting version 26 and pressing update changes the button to Publish and fails; no deployment logs are visible to troubleshoot; asking the in-product AI to rebuild with no design changes charged 275+ credits and produced no rebuild and no new version, leaving them about 280 credits down. Two screenshots show the <domain> domain modal with a green Connected badge and the banner "We could not load your domain ownership. Retry before removing this domain."

**Evidence snapshot (2026-09-18, commit 36f37d386abadd67452b6889cf446ef226fad560)**: website row deployment_status = failed, deployment_error `Command "bun run build" exited with 1`, custom_domain <domain>, domain_verified true. Blast radius from production: 20 live website rows across 18 organizations are in deployment_status failed, 7 of those organizations also carry a verified custom domain. Code path: `publishWebsiteDeployment` in apps/web/lib/website/publish-website-deployment.ts persists deploymentStatus 'pending' in the same update that stores the new vercelDeploymentId; `website.checkDeploymentStatus` in apps/web/trpc/routers/website/web-core.ts writes 'failed' with the provider error message; the redeploy-after-domain-connect Inngest function returns mode 'skip' whenever deploymentStatus is 'failed'. The customer-facing message is a constant, PUBLISHED_WEBSITE_SAFE_DEPLOYMENT_ERROR in apps/web/lib/website/published-website-url.ts returned by getWebsiteDeploymentErrorMessage for any failed deployment, which discards the persisted build error; apps/web/components/ai-website-creator/publish-control.tsx renders it. Overlapping open work: parent master ENG-13921 and its child ENG-13920 cover the never-published plus verified-domain-shown-as-connected coupling, ENG-12240 and the canceled SAN-42 cover this exact publish failure string, and ENG-10093 covers hardening the publish flow.

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 1 preview renders blank/white screen
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The AI Name 1 preview renders a blank/white canvas instead of the generated site, so customers cannot review their site before publishing. Recurring across multiple workspaces.

## Problem

A customer opens the Name 1 and the chrome loads, but the preview canvas stays blank/white, blocking review and publish. Reproduced via impersonation (not browser-specific).

## Root cause

The generated website's preview fails to render: the preview iframe (apps/web/components/website-builder/preview-panel.tsx) points at the site's v0 preview_url, which serves a blank page. The specific import/build error in the generated site is not yet pinned (the website agent's chat asks for the browser console error); ENG-12505 surfaced a "zod safeParseAsync" import error in the same symptom.

## Blast radius

1 org confirmed (counted 2026-09-08). Recurring symptom also reported in ENG-12505 and ENG-9943; exact affected count not yet measured.

## Proposed fix

Identify the import/build error in the generated site that produces the blank preview, and either steer generation away from it (as ENG-13149 does for sonner/spinner imports) or harden the preview to surface the error instead of a blank canvas.

## What's included

Root-cause fix for the blank preview. Related: ENG-12505 (same symptom), ENG-9943 (black screen). Not included: the credit refund (ENG-13577).

## Regression seam

Opening a generated site's preview renders the site; a failing build surfaces an error message instead of a blank canvas.

## Done when

* The preview renders the generated site (no blank canvas).
* A failing generated build shows a visible error, not a blank screen.
* A regression test proves the preview render path.

## Reports

* ENG-13578

relatedSnapshot.title: AI Name 1 redeploys serve PNG images as base64 data-URI strings, breaking image loading
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom source**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Conversation context**: Customer reports that every time his AI Name 1 site generates or he saves a change, the site's images (including the logo) stop showing and the browser network tab reports a 206 response. He sees broken image placeholders where the hero and logo should be, and he believes a compiler/CI-CD change at ~12pm CST caused it. It reproduces on both manual edits and AI edits.

**Testable claim**: When an AI Name 1 site (v0/agent-git build path) is generated, edited, or redeployed, PNG image files reach the published Vercel site as undecoded base64 data-URI text, so the browser cannot render them and reports a 206 partial-content response.

**Root cause**: The published image file is served with its entire body being the literal string `data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...` (UTF-8, ~2.7 MB for the hero). Correct deployments write the decoded binary PNG bytes (`8910 4E47...`). This is a pass-through of a base64 data-URI into a binary-only image path on publish/redeploy, not a change we shipped; the string originates upstream (the external generation provider returning image content as a data URI) and is not decoded before being written to the deployed image asset. Confirmed contrast: another v0 site on Vercel serves the same image type as proper binary PNG.

**Evidence**: live fetch of <url:vercel.app> returns HTTP 200 body whose first bytes are `data:image/png;base64,` and last bytes include `==`; a Range request returns `206` with `Content-Range` and a 1-byte body of `d`. Production DB `website_file` for this organization shows image files whose `content` begins with `data:image/`. `decodeFileContent` in `apps/web/lib/v0/template-zip.ts` handles data URIs for template zips, but no equivalent decode exists in the agent-git commit/v0-conversion write path (`apps/web/lib/website-agent/v0-conversion.ts`, `apps/web/lib/website-agent/commit.ts`).

**Blast radius**: production has 20 image files (PNG/JPG/WEBP/GIF) whose stored content is a `data:image/...` URI, across 2 organizations; 1,721 live-or-historical v0 websites across 899 organizations use this build path.

**Labels**: intercom-sourced, Customer reported

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: AI Name 1 publish failure hides the build error and leaves a stale failure state after recovery
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A failed AI Name 1 production build leaves the customer with no way to find out why. The publish panel replaces the real build failure with a fixed string, and a site that later publishes successfully keeps the old failure recorded on it. Customers whose generated site has a compile error cannot tell whether they are looking at their own broken code or a platform problem.

## Problem

When a version's production build fails, the customer sees only "Publishing failed. Please try again." There is no build error, no build log, and no route to either. The help center tells them to check the version for a build error and to send support "the error shown", which the product cannot show them. Separately, after a failed publish the site keeps the old failure on record even once a later publish succeeds, so the row that reports state to the product is wrong about the site.

## Root cause

`getWebsiteDeploymentErrorMessage` in `apps/web/lib/website/published-website-url.ts` returns the constant `PUBLISHED_WEBSITE_SAFE_DEPLOYMENT_ERROR` for every website whose `deploymentStatus` is `failed`, so the persisted `deployment_error` is discarded before the UI sees it. `apps/web/components/ai-website-creator/publish-control.tsx` renders that constant and has no build-error or build-log surface in the failed presentation. Separately, the READY branch of `website.checkDeploymentStatus` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/website/web-core.ts` writes `deploymentStatus: 'deployed'` and `deploymentUrl` without clearing `deploymentError`, so a recovered row keeps a stale failure. The publish path itself is not gated on the failed state, so the customer is not actually blocked from retrying.

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected (30-day window, re-counted 2026-09-22): 3 live website rows across 3 organizations sit in `deployment_status = 'failed'`, all 3 also holding a verified custom domain. The window figure was 5 rows across 5 organizations on 2026-09-18, so failed rows are being recovered as well as added. All-time, without a window: 18 rows across 16 organizations, oldest 2026-05-19 by `updated_at` (2026-04-21 by `created_at`). Stale-state evidence: 32 live rows are `deployed` while still carrying a `bun run build` error, so the stale-failure path has fired at least that many times. Query: counts over `website` for `deployment_status = 'failed' and deleted_at is null`, the same restricted to `updated_at > now() - interval '30 days'`, and `deployment_status = 'deployed' and deployment_error ilike '%bun run build%'`. Counted 2026-09-18 against production. Users are not counted separately: the row's owner is nullable and is not a reliable unit. Potentially exposed: 947 organizations hold at least one live website row (1844 rows) and therefore traverse the publish path.

## Proposed fix

A failed publish should tell the customer why, and a successful publish should leave no trace of an earlier failure. Concretely: on `deployment_status = 'failed'`, the publish surface shows the recorded reason and a path to the build log rather than a fixed string, and any successful publish clears the previous `deployment_error`.

## What's included

In scope: the user-visible failure disclosure on publish failure, and clearing stale failure state on success. Out of scope: the site-specific compile error that triggers an individual build failure, which is repaired per site. Related, not owned here: the publish-flow hardening plan that already lists these acceptance criteria, and the duplicate publish-failure report already in triage.

## Regression seam

Trigger: a website row whose `deploymentStatus` is `failed` with a recorded `deployment_error`, and a publish that reaches READY after a failure. Observable red-before, green-after: the failed publish surface shows the recorded reason instead of the fixed string, and the recovered row ends with no `deployment_error`. Seam: the publish-control failed-state tests under `apps/web/tests/components/ai-website-creator/`, plus the unit tests beside `apps/web/lib/website/published-website-url.ts`.

## Done when

* A publish that fails on its production build shows the customer the recorded reason and a route to the build log, not a fixed string.
* A publish that succeeds after an earlier failure leaves no `deployment_error` on the row.
* A regression test proves both behaviours at the named seam.

## Reports

* (child reports are linked by the parent relation)

Fixes preview environment login failures and removes console.debug statement as requested.

Preview environments use isolated Neon database branches that contain schema but **no data**. The allowlist tables (`allowlist_email`, `allowlist_domain`) are empty, causing all email validation to fail and users to be redirected to the marketing funnel.

* **File**: `scripts/seed-preview-allowlist.ts`
* **Command**: `pnpm db:seed-preview-allowlist`
* Populates common email domains (gmail.com, outlook.com, etc.) in preview environments

* Name 6 steps and prevention strategies
* Long-term solution recommendations

relatedSnapshot.title: Workflow publish rejects duplicate labels without attempting auto-fix
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Bug

The `publish` mutation in `trpc/routers/workflows.ts` calls `validateUniqueNodeLabels` directly on raw `draftNodes` without first running `deduplicateWorkflowLabels`. This means any workflow that contains duplicate step labels — including workflows created before ENG-6129 shipped or imported from external sources — will throw a `BAD_REQUEST` and be permanently unpublishable, with no automatic resolution.

The `restoreVersion` mutation (line \~3687 in the same file) already does this correctly: it calls `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` before `validateUniqueNodeLabels`. The `publish` path should match.

**Affected file:** `trpc/routers/workflows.ts`

## Reproduction

1. Create a workflow with two steps that share the same label (e.g. via import or by directly editing `draftNodes` in the DB before ENG-6129 shipped).
2. Attempt to publish the workflow.
3. Observe: `BAD_REQUEST` — "Cannot publish workflow with duplicate step names".
4. There is no UI path to auto-resolve; the user must manually rename each duplicate step.

## Fix

In the `publish` mutation, before calling `validateUniqueNodeLabels`, run `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` on the nodes — exactly as `restoreVersion` does.

```ts
// trpc/routers/workflows.ts — publish mutation (~line 1503)

// Before (current):
const nodes = Array.isArray(workflow.draftNodes) ? workflow.draftNodes : [];
// ...
validateUniqueNodeLabels(nodes, 'Cannot publish workflow with duplicate step names');

// After:
const rawNodes = Array.isArray(workflow.draftNodes) ? workflow.draftNodes : [];
const validNodes = rawNodes.filter(
  (n): n is Parameters<typeof deduplicateWorkflowLabels>[0][number] =>
    typeof n === 'object' && n !== null && 'id' in n && 'data' in n &&
    typeof (n as Record<string, unknown>).data === 'object' &&
    (n as Record<string, unknown>).data !== null
);
const nodes = deduplicateWorkflowLabels(validNodes) as typeof rawNodes;
validateUniqueNodeLabels(nodes, 'Cannot publish workflow with duplicate step names');
```

Only change the `publish` mutation. Do not touch `updateDraft`, `restoreVersion`, or any other path.

## Tests

Add a unit test to the workflows router test suite (or integration test) that:

* Sets up a workflow whose `draftNodes` contains two nodes with the same label.
* Calls the `publish` mutation.
* Asserts it succeeds (does not throw) and that the published nodes have deduplicated labels.

---

## Implementation Plan (Name 7)

### Summary of Current Code

* **Background**: The workflow system has a publish mutation that validates and snapshots the current draft into a versioned record. ENG-6129 (commit `778f2f395`, PR #2863) added `validateUniqueNodeLabels` to reject duplicate step names, and `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` to auto-fix them.
* **Current Behavior**: The `publish` mutation (line \~1503) reads raw `draftNodes` and calls `validateUniqueNodeLabels` directly — no deduplication step. Workflows with duplicate labels permanently fail to publish.
* **Key Components**: `validateUniqueNodeLabels` (line 516), `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` (imported at line 48), `restoreVersion` (line \~3675, correct reference implementation).

### Affected Files

1. `trpc/routers/workflows.ts` — Modify publish mutation (lines 1503-1524): rename `nodes` to `rawNodes`, add type guard filter + `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` call before validation.
2. `tests/trpc/routers/workflows.test.ts` — Add test: workflow with duplicate label draftNodes → publish succeeds → version nodes have deduplicated labels.

### System Overview

* Publish mutation flow: fetch workflow → extract draftNodes → validate integrations → **\[insert dedup here\]** → validate unique labels → extract trigger configs → create version (DB) → sync triggers → update workflow status.
* The `nodes` variable flows through the entire mutation. Name 8 nodes propagate to version creation and all downstream processing.
* `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` is already imported; no new dependencies needed.

### Edge Cases

* Type guard filter narrows `unknown[]` to `WorkflowNode[]` — invalid entries dropped (same as `restoreVersion`).
* Note nodes skipped by `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` (correct behavior).
* Triple+ duplicates handled via incrementing suffixes ("Step (2)", "Step (3)").
* No draftNodes write-back — deduplicated labels only appear in the published version record.

### Key Considerations

* Follow exact pattern from `restoreVersion` (lines 3675-3688).
* `as typeof rawNodes` cast maintains type compatibility with downstream consumers.
* Minimal, targeted fix — no architectural changes.

### Suggested Approach

1. Modify publish mutation: rename `nodes` → `rawNodes`, add filter + dedup, reassign to `nodes`.
2. Add unit test with duplicate-label draftNodes → assert publish succeeds and version has unique labels.
3. Run lint + typecheck.

### Confidence Assessment

* **Overall Confidence**: High
* **Completeness**: \~95% of relevant code reviewed
* **Open-endedness**: Minimal — only design decision is not writing deduplicated nodes back to `draftNodes` (matching current publish behavior and ticket scope)

---

## Codebase Verification

Confirmed in codebase:

* `trpc/routers/workflows.ts` line 48: `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` is already imported — no new import needed
* `trpc/routers/workflows.ts` lines 1503–1524: `publish` mutation reads `workflow.draftNodes` directly into `nodes` and calls `validateUniqueNodeLabels(nodes, ...)` with no dedup step — exact match to bug description
* `trpc/routers/workflows.ts` lines 3675–3688: `restoreVersion` uses the correct pattern (type guard filter → `deduplicateWorkflowLabels` → `validateUniqueNodeLabels`) — confirmed reference implementation
* `tests/trpc/routers/workflows.test.ts`: integration test suite uses a real test DB via Testcontainers; existing `publish` test at line 188 provides the scaffolding pattern for the new test
* No open PR on this branch

**Agent feasibility:** ✅ Feasible. Scope is 2 files. Requirements are unambiguous with a clear reference implementation in the same file. Meaningful integration test can be written using the existing test infrastructure. No external services. In the Workflows project — highest priority per sprint instructions.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add questions for existing case studies to the onboarding flow
relatedSnapshot.description:
We need to capture case studies in the onboarding flow to properly generate Direct method emails in the Campaign Agent.

### Problem

Currently, the onboarding flow does not collect information about the user's existing case studies, testimonials, or success stories. This information is critical for the Campaign Agent to generate personalized Direct method emails that reference real client results and build credibility with prospects.

### User Story

As a user going through onboarding, I want to provide information about my successful client case studies so that the Campaign Agent can leverage these real results when crafting personalized outreach emails.

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] Add a new onboarding step/section dedicated to case studies
- [ ] Include form fields for:
  - Client name (or "Client A" for anonymity)
  - Industry/vertical of the client
  - Initial problem/challenge faced
  - Solution provided
  - Quantifiable results achieved (metrics, percentages, revenue impact, etc.)
  - Timeframe (how long to achieve results)
  - Optional: Client testimonial quote
- [ ] Support adding multiple case studies (minimum 1, recommend 3-5)
- [ ] Store case study data in the database linked to the user's profile
- [ ] Make case studies accessible to the Campaign Agent for email generation
- [ ] Add validation to ensure required fields are completed
- [ ] Include helpful prompts/examples to guide users on what information to provide

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Users can add, edit, and remove case studies during onboarding
- [ ] At least one case study is required to complete onboarding
- [ ] Case study data is successfully saved to the database with proper user association
- [ ] Campaign Agent can retrieve and utilize case study information when generating Direct method emails
- [ ] Form validation prevents submission of incomplete case studies
- [ ] UI/UX is intuitive with clear instructions and examples
- [ ] Case studies display properly in review/summary step before onboarding completion
- [ ] System handles edge cases (very long text, special characters, etc.)

### Technical Considerations

* Database schema updates needed for case study storage
* API endpoints for CRUD operations on case studies
* Integration with Campaign Agent's email generation logic
* Proper data sanitization and validation
* Consider privacy/anonymization options for sensitive client information

## Out of Scope

* Importing case studies from external sources (PDF, LinkedIn, etc.)
* AI-assisted case study writing or enhancement
* Public gallery or sharing of case studies between users
* Advanced formatting options (images, videos, rich text)
* Integration with CRM systems to auto-populate case study data

relatedSnapshot.title: Store preview, publish, and version history
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Build Store Preview and Publish Flow — Version History with Rollback ### Context This feature complements the store builder editor (ENG-7115) by adding a complete publish workflow: preview draft changes before going live, version history tracking with every publish, and the ability to rollback to any previous version. This ensures store owners can confidently make changes knowing they can always revert if something goes wrong. The publish flow follows a **draft → preview → publish** pattern where all edits are saved as drafts, previewed in context, and only made live when the user explicitly publishes. Each publish creates a versioned snapshot that can be restored later. --- ### Database Schema **New table:** `commerceStoreVersion` — add to `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts`: ```typescript export const commerceStoreVersionTable = pgTable( 'commerce_store_version', { ...getBaseColumnsWithOrganization(), pageId: uuid('page_id').notNull().references(() => commerceStorePageTable.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }), version: integer('version').notNull(), // auto-incrementing per page, calculated as MAX(version) + 1 sections: jsonb('sections').$type().notNull(), // full snapshot of sections at publish time publishedAt: timestamp('published_at', { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(), publishedBy: uuid('published_by').references(() => userTable.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }), }, (table) => [ index('commerce_store_version_page_idx').on(table.pageId), uniqueIndex('commerce_store_version_page_version_idx').on(table.pageId, table.version), ] ); ``` **Key design decisions:** * `version` is an integer that auto-increments per page (not globally) — calculated at insert time via `SELECT MAX(version) + 1` * `sections` stores a complete JSONB snapshot of the sections array at the time of publish — no diffs, full snapshot for simplicity and reliable rollback * `publishedBy` references the user who triggered the publish, with `SET NULL` on delete so versions survive user deletion * `pageId` has `CASCADE` delete — if the page is deleted, all its versions are cleaned up * Unique index on `(pageId, version)` prevents duplicate version numbers * Follows the same pattern as `websiteVersionTable` in `lib/db/schema/website-version.ts` **Relation to** `commerceStorePageTable` (from ENG-7115): * `commerceStorePageTable.publishedVersionId` references the currently live version * `commerceStorePageTable.sections` = the live sections (copied from draft at publish time) * `commerceStorePageTable.draftSections` = in-progress edits (null when no unpublished changes) --- ### tRPC Procedures **Extend** `trpc/routers/commerce/store-builder.ts` with these additional procedures: #### `publishPage` (mutation) Full publish flow — this is the most critical procedure: ``` Input: { slug: string } Steps: 1. Get current page by slug + orgId (from context) 2. Verify draftSections is not null (there must be unpublished changes to publish) 3. Calculate next version number: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 FROM commerce_store_version WHERE page_id = ? 4. Insert version snapshot: INSERT INTO commerce_store_version (pageId, version, sections, publishedBy) VALUES (page.id, nextVersion, page.draftSections, ctx.user.id) 5. Update the page atomically: UPDATE commerce_store_page SET sections = draftSections, draftSections = NULL, isPublished = true, publishedAt = NOW(), publishedVersionId = newVersion.id WHERE id = page.id 6. Return { version: nextVersion, publishedAt: new Date() } ``` All steps should run in a single database transaction to ensure atomicity. #### `listVersions` (query) ``` Input: { pageId: string } Output: Array of { id, version, publishedAt, publishedBy: { id, name, image } } - Join on user table for publisher name and avatar - Sort by version DESC (newest first) - Paginate with cursor-based pagination (optional for MVP, limit 50) ``` #### `rollbackToVersion` (mutation) ``` Input: { versionId: string } Steps: 1. Load the version record by ID, verify it belongs to a page in the user's org 2. Set the version's sections as the page's draftSections: UPDATE commerce_store_page SET draftSections = version.sections WHERE id = version.pageId 3. Return the restored sections so the builder can immediately display them ``` **Important:** Rollback does NOT directly update the live `sections`. It loads the old version as a **draft** so the user can review and optionally edit before re-publishing. This prevents accidental live changes. #### `getPreviewData` (query) ``` Input: { slug: string } Output: { sections: StoreSection[], isPublished: boolean, hasDraft: boolean } - Returns draftSections if they exist (for preview), otherwise returns published sections - Used by the preview route/panel to render the current state ``` --- ### Publish Flow UI (in Store Builder) The publish controls live in a **toolbar** at the top of the store builder page, between the header and the three-panel layout. **Name 12 buttons:** | Button | Condition | Action | | -- | -- | -- | | **Save Draft** | Always visible | Explicitly saves current sections to `draftSections`. Note: auto-save (from ENG-7115) already handles this, but an explicit button provides user confidence. | | **Publish** | Active only when `draftSections !== null` (has unpublished changes) | Calls `publishPage` mutation → shows success toast "Published! Version X is now live." | | **Discard Changes** | Active only when `draftSections !== null` | Confirmation dialog: "Discard all unpublished changes? This will revert to the last published version." → calls `discardDraft` → reloads published sections into editor. | | **History** | Always visible | Opens the version history Sheet (right-side drawer). | | **Preview** | Always visible | Opens full-page preview in a new tab. | **Visual indicators:** * Show a badge/dot on the "Publish" button when there are unpublished changes * Show "Draft" badge in the toolbar when editing unpublished changes * Show "Published" badge with relative timestamp when no draft exists --- ### Version History UI **Component:** `components/commerce/store-builder/VersionHistorySheet.tsx` Opens as a `Sheet` (from ` at /components/ui/sheet`) sliding in from the right side, triggered by the "History" button in the toolbar. **Layout:** ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ │ Version History [X] │ ├─────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ v3 (Current) LIVE │ │ │ │ Published 2 hours ago │ │ │ │ by Name 10 │ │ │ │ [Rollback] │ │ ← disabled for current version │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ v2 │ │ │ │ Published 3 days ago │ │ │ │ by Jane Smith │ │ │ │ [Rollback] │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ v1 │ │ │ │ Published Name 11 15, 2026 │ │ │ │ by Name 10 │ │ │ │ [Rollback] │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Each version row shows:** * Version number (e.g., "v3") * "LIVE" badge (using ``) on the version matching `publishedVersionId` * Relative timestamp using `formatDistanceToNow` from `date-fns` (e.g., "2 hours ago", "3 days ago") * Publisher name and avatar * "Rollback" button — disabled for the currently live version **Rollback flow:** 1. User clicks "Rollback" on a version 2. Confirmation dialog appears: "Restore version X? This will load the sections from version X as a draft. You can review the changes and publish when ready." 3. On confirm: call `rollbackToVersion` mutation 4. Close the Sheet 5. Builder loads the restored sections as the current draft 6. User can now edit further or publish immediately 7. Show toast: "Version X restored as draft. Publish to make it live." --- ### Preview Implementation **Option A (Recommended for MVP): Name 13 preview in builder center panel** The center panel of the three-panel layout (from ENG-7115) already renders section renderers inline. This serves as the primary preview. No additional work needed for basic preview. **Option B: Full-page preview in new tab** For a more accurate representation of how the storefront will look: 1. **"Open Preview" button** in the toolbar opens a new browser tab 2. **Preview route:** `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/store-builder/preview/page.tsx` 3. This page renders a full-width storefront preview (no builder chrome) using `getPreviewData` 4. **Preview banner:** A fixed-position bar at the top of the preview page: ```tsx
Preview These changes are not live yet
``` 5. The preview page adds `padding-top` to account for the banner height 6. Preview renders `draftSections` if available, otherwise falls back to published `sections` --- ### Component Structure ``` components/commerce/store-builder/ ├── PublishToolbar.tsx — toolbar with Save Draft, Publish, Discard, History, Preview buttons ├── VersionHistorySheet.tsx — Sheet with version list, rollback actions ├── VersionHistoryItem.tsx — individual version row in the history list ├── RollbackConfirmDialog.tsx — confirmation dialog for rollback action ├── DiscardDraftDialog.tsx — confirmation dialog for discarding unpublished changes ├── PreviewBanner.tsx — fixed banner shown on full-page preview ("Changes are not live") └── PublishSuccessToast.tsx — (optional) custom toast content showing version number ``` --- ### State Management **Draft detection:** ```typescript const hasDraft = page.draftSections !== null; const isPublished = page.isPublished; ``` **Publish button state:** * Disabled when `!hasDraft` (nothing to publish) * Shows loading spinner during `publishPage` mutation * After success: invalidate `getPage` query, close any open editors, show toast **Optimistic updates:** * On publish: optimistically set `draftSections = null` and `sections = draftSections` in the query cache * On discard: optimistically set `draftSections = null` and reload `sections` from cache * On rollback: optimistically set `draftSections = restoredSections` in the query cache --- ### Codebase Reference Table | What | File | Pattern to Follow | | -- | -- | -- | | Version table pattern | `lib/db/schema/website-version.ts` | Status enum, snapshot JSONB storage, version numbering | | Deployment pattern | `lib/db/schema/website-deployment.ts` | Provider enum, status tracking (reference only) | | Preview panel | `components/website-builder/preview-panel.tsx` | iframe with sandbox, postMessage sync (for future iframe approach) | | Sheet component | ` at /components/ui/sheet` | Right-side drawer for version history | | Name 14 component | ` at /components/ui/dialog` | Rollback and discard confirmation dialogs | | Badge | ` at /components/ui/badge` | `variant="success"` for LIVE, `variant="warning"` for Draft/Preview | | Button | ` at /components/ui/button` | Name 12 buttons with variant and size props | | Toast | `sonner` / ` at /components/ui/sonner` | Success/error notifications | | formatDistanceToNow | `date-fns` | Relative timestamps in version history (e.g., "2 hours ago") | | Schema | `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts` | Add `commerceStoreVersionTable` alongside the page table | | tRPC router | `trpc/routers/commerce/store-builder.ts` | Extend with publish/version/rollback procedures | | Transaction pattern | Existing tRPC mutations | `db.transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` for atomic publish | | Page layout | ` at /components/ui/page` | `Page`, `PageHeader`, `PageBody` for preview page | | User join | `lib/db/schema/user.ts` | Join `userTable` for publisher name in version list | --- ### Implementation Steps 1. **Add** `commerceStoreVersionTable` to `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts` with the schema above. Export from `lib/db/schema/index.ts`. Define Drizzle relations to `commerceStorePageTable` and `userTable`. 2. **Run** `bun db:generate` to create the migration, then `bun db:migrate` to apply it. 3. **Add** `publishPage` procedure to the store builder tRPC router — implement the full 6-step publish flow inside a database transaction. 4. **Add** `listVersions` procedure — query with user join, sorted by version DESC. 5. **Add** `rollbackToVersion` procedure — load version, set as draftSections on the page. 6. **Add** `getPreviewData` procedure — return draftSections or sections based on availability. 7. **Build** `PublishToolbar.tsx` — toolbar component with all 5 buttons, proper disabled states, and loading indicators. 8. **Integrate toolbar** into `StoreBuilderPage.tsx` (from ENG-7115) — place between the page header and the three-panel layout. 9. **Build** `VersionHistorySheet.tsx` — Sheet component that fetches and displays version list. 10. **Build** `VersionHistoryItem.tsx` — individual version row with version number, relative date, publisher info, LIVE badge, and rollback button. 11. **Build** `RollbackConfirmDialog.tsx` — confirmation dialog with clear messaging about what rollback does (loads as draft, not direct publish). 12. **Build** `DiscardDraftDialog.tsx` — confirmation dialog for discarding unpublished changes. 13. **Implement rollback flow** — on confirm, call mutation, close sheet, update builder state, show toast. 14. **Build preview page** at `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/store-builder/preview/page.tsx` — full-width storefront rendering with preview banner. 15. **Build** `PreviewBanner.tsx` — fixed-position warning banner for preview mode. 16. **Add optimistic updates** — update TanStack Query cache on publish, discard, and rollback for instant UI feedback. 17. **Update** `scripts/dump-preview-data.sh` — add `dump_copy` lines for both `commerce_store_page` and `commerce_store_version` tables. 18. **Test the full publish cycle** — create draft → preview → publish → verify version created → rollback → verify draft loaded → re-publish. --- ### Verification Checklist - [ ] `commerceStoreVersionTable` migration runs cleanly on a fresh database - [ ] Unique index on `(pageId, version)` prevents duplicate version numbers - [ ] `publishPage` creates a version snapshot with correct version number (incrementing from previous max) - [ ] `publishPage` atomically updates `sections`, clears `draftSections`, sets `isPublished`, and links `publishedVersionId` - [ ] `publishPage` runs in a transaction — if any step fails, nothing is committed - [ ] `publishPage` rejects if `draftSections` is null (nothing to publish) - [ ] `listVersions` returns versions sorted newest-first with publisher name and avatar - [ ] `listVersions` correctly identifies the currently live version via `publishedVersionId` - [ ] `rollbackToVersion` loads old sections as `draftSections` (NOT directly to live `sections`) - [ ] `rollbackToVersion` verifies the version belongs to a page in the user's organization - [ ] Publish button is disabled when there are no unpublished changes - [ ] Discard Changes button is disabled when there are no unpublished changes - [ ] Rollback button is disabled for the currently live version in the history list - [ ] Confirmation dialogs appear before rollback and discard actions - [ ] Toast notifications show on publish success, rollback success, and discard success - [ ] Version history Sheet loads and displays all versions for the current page - [ ] Preview page renders draft sections with the preview warning banner - [ ] Preview banner clearly communicates that changes are not live - [ ] Optimistic updates provide instant feedback on publish/discard/rollback - [ ] `scripts/dump-preview-data.sh` updated with new tables - [ ] No ` at /lib/env` imports in any client components - [ ] All logging uses `logger` from ` at /lib/logger` (not console) - [ ] All database queries are scoped to the authenticated user's organization

Create "portfolio" page with company pages based on our case studies
Add guided expression builder with live preview and validation
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Template/expression authoring remains error-prone and less discoverable than n8n-style expression workflows.

## Root Cause

Expressions are supported, but authoring relies heavily on manual typing and post-failure correction rather than guided construction and live evaluation.

## Example of how it'll cause issues

A user references the wrong upstream field path, publishes successfully, then discovers failures at runtime due to invalid expression output.

## Plan for solution

1. Add expression builder UI with node/field picker and operator helpers.
2. Add live preview/evaluation using latest run data and/or mock input.
3. Add inline validation with actionable error messages before run/publish.
4. Support quick insert from output schema and copy-safe path generation.
5. Add unit/integration tests for expression serialization and preview correctness.

relatedSnapshot.title: Harden API validation, domain edge cases, and idempotency
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Bad input, duplicate requests, weird domains, race conditions, and unsafe worker URLs can turn normal customer behavior or abuse into routing bugs, cert issues, or service crashes.

## Solution

Add strict runtime validation, explicit edge-case handling, and idempotent behavior for domain lifecycle APIs.

## Technical implementation details

* Add runtime schemas for API request bodies, environment config, domain input, worker names, and worker URLs using Zod or another lightweight validator.
* Validate missing fields, invalid JSON, unsupported methods, wrong content type, oversized bodies, malformed hostnames, duplicate domains, bad auth, and invalid worker URLs.
* Harden domain normalization for uppercase input, trailing dots, whitespace, `www.` input, apex/subdomain handling, punycode/IDN, invalid characters, and long hostnames.
* Prevent customer domains from claiming platform hosts such as staging/production ingress hosts or `acquisity.ai` control domains.
* Define idempotent create behavior: same domain and same funnel returns existing record or a clean conflict; same domain and different funnel returns conflict.
* Add database unique constraints and code handling for concurrent domain creation.
* Add tests for duplicate creates, concurrent creates, repeated DNS checks, and invalid inputs.
* Ensure all validation failures return controlled `400`/`409` responses instead of crashing the router.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add compile-time workflow validator before publish and run
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Invalid workflow definitions are often discovered at runtime, causing avoidable production failures.

## Root Cause

Validation is currently incomplete and not enforced as a full preflight compile step across graph semantics, step configuration, and expression references.

## Example of how it'll cause issues

A workflow with unresolved variable paths or invalid branch structure is published successfully and only fails once a customer-triggered run executes.

## Plan for solution

1. Implement a compile/validate phase that runs before publish and run.
2. Validate graph integrity (single trigger, reachable nodes, valid joins, no illegal cycles).
3. Validate step configuration schemas and required connections.
4. Validate expression references against known upstream outputs where possible.
5. Return actionable error diagnostics in the editor with node-level pointers.
